thread:
Amanda: Drafting the PRD for quota/metering & billing semantics. Need quick decisions on per-project vs per-api-key billing, enforcement modes (soft/hard), and meter granularity (raw tokens vs billed-chunks). Can reviewers take a look today?

Josh: I can. Quick perf question: do we rely on existing rate-limit headers for telemetry, or add a canonical usage API for reconciliation and UI?

Samir: We need both. Headers are realtime-friendly but not authoritative. Spec a /v1/usage (hourly/daily aggregates) as the source of truth for billing, with a webhook/event stream for reconciliation. Dedicated customers should get historical backfill.

Liz: Proposed acceptance criteria: 1) UI shows per-route + per-model remaining quota for current window; 2) /v1/usage returns hourly aggregates for 90 days; 3) soft enforcement = allow requests but emit warning header + billing event; 4) hard enforcement = 429 until quota reset or purchase.

Kevin: Edge cases: mid-cycle downgrades must be prorated (no retro charge). Multi-region concurrent traffic needs consistent global quota enforcement keyed to customer_id. Also consider clock skew and eventual consistency windows.

Amanda: Product preference: default to soft enforcement for self-serve, enterprise can opt into hard. For soft, don't return 206. Use normal 200 but add a clear warning header and emit a quota.soft_reached event. If blocking, return 429.

Samir: Agreed. Events: quota.soft_reached, quota.hard_blocked, quota.topup. /v1/usage should be queryable by project/api_key, model, and route. Also include tokenization metadata (tokenizer version) in usage rows.

Josh: SDK change: helper to surface quota headers and parse Retry-After + advisory fields. Proposed headers:

X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 123456
X-Redwood-Quota-Limit: 1000000
X-Redwood-Quota-Window-Reset: 1710000000
X-Redwood-Quota-State: soft|hard
X-Redwood-Tokenizer: redwood-v1

Amanda: API prototype for admin quota creation (Dedicated/Private UI):
```
POST /v1/quotas
{
  "scope": "project",
  "quota_units": "tokens",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "window": "30d",
  "enforcement": "soft",
  "rollover": false
}
```

Liz: Launch checklist draft: PRD + API spec, UI mockups + panel, SDK helpers, enforcement regression tests (soft->hard transitions), 3-customer canary, billing reconciliation test harness, and docs with backoff guidance.

Kevin: Performance design: local cache-first enforcement with central fallback. Keep local TTL short and use leaky-bucket counters locally to avoid p99 spikes. Instrument cache hit rate; if central unavailable, fallback to conservative defaults and emit incident metric.

Amanda: Prioritization candidate for roadmap: High: core /v1/usage + SDK parsing + enforcement events; High: enterprise hard switch + audit logs; Medium: UI per-route panels + prorate logic; Medium: mid-cycle plan UX.

Samir: Tokenization edge-case: hosted vs on-prem tokenizers may diverge. Billing must use platform tokenizer (deterministic) and publish SDK function to compute billed tokens. Add tokenization_version string in usage rows to resolve disputes.

Josh: Client retry semantics: provide Retry-After and recommend jittered exponential backoff in docs to avoid thundering herd when many clients hit soft/hard boundaries. Add tests that simulate mass retries.

Amanda: Action items: @Josh draft header + SDK surface by Wed; @Samir spec /v1/usage + events; @Liz mock UI + acceptance criteria; @Kevin design cache + fallback; Amanda will assemble PRD draft and circulate. Signoff needed by Friday EOD for sprint inclusion.

deploy-bot: Please add RFC label `quota-metering-prd` and set reviewers to @Amanda @Josh @Samir.

Liz: I'll attach mock screenshots to the PRD and call out mid-cycle and multi-region failure modes in the acceptance section.

Amanda: Thanks all. If no blocking objections, I'll publish the first draft EOD and open the RFC thread.
